attacks.claim: A partial class marked [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] that implements IMessagePackFormatter<T> for a type T from another assembly gets its Serialize and Deserialize members generated in the consuming project.
attacks.scenario: If the type T is an inaccessible type (e.g., an `internal` type from another assembly), the generator will reject it and report MsgPack021 instead of generating the members.
attacks.test_sketch: Declare an `internal class InternalType` in Project A. In Project B, declare `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class Formatter : IMessagePackFormatter<InternalType>`. The generator will emit MsgPack021 and not generate the members.
attacks.result_detail: describes documented or already tested behaviour (MsgPack021 / MsgPack022 paths); no probe written

attacks.claim: Without a surrogate, the generated formatter writes every public read-write instance property and field of T as a string-keyed map entry named after the member.
attacks.scenario: If the type T has a public read-write indexer property, it is explicitly skipped and not written as a map entry.
attacks.test_sketch: Define `class T { public int this[int key] { get => 0; set { } } }`. Generate a formatter without a surrogate. The indexer is not serialized.
attacks.result_detail: G4: an indexer is skipped and the type serializes as {"Id":9}. Intended. runs/2129/probe/G4_IndexerIsSkipped.txt

attacks.claim: Attributes that are present on T are used for the wire contract.
attacks.scenario: Attributes on T are completely ignored by the generator when using `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]`. For example, a property marked with `[IgnoreMember]` on T will still be serialized.
attacks.test_sketch: Define `class T { [IgnoreMember] public int X { get; set; } }`. Generate a formatter for T without a surrogate. The property `X` is serialized, proving the attribute on T was ignored.
attacks.result_detail: G1: [IgnoreMember] on a member of the formatted type is ignored; the member X is written. runs/2129/probe/G1_IgnoreMemberOnFormattedType.txt

attacks.claim: The generated resolver registers each generated formatter, so GeneratedMessagePackResolver.Instance returns it for the formatted type.
The fixture assembly that declares the formatted types has no MessagePack reference, so the feature works without adding anything to the assembly that owns T.

Hand-written formatters and existing generated formatters are unaffected: the exclusion in the formatter search only matches classes carrying the new attribute, and the template keeps 'internal sealed class' for every other formatter.
The new attribute, the four analyzer diagnostics and the surrogate option are documented in the README, in per-diagnostic pages and in the analyzer release notes.
Only public read-write members are written. Read-only members and members with a non-public setter are skipped, and no diagnostic says so.
attacks.scenario: If a surrogate type is used and it includes a member that matches a read-only member on the formatted type, the generator reports a diagnostic (MsgPack022).
attacks.test_sketch: Define `class T { public int ReadOnlyProp { get; } }` and a surrogate `class Surrogate { [Key(0)] public int ReadOnlyProp { get; set; } }`. The generator will emit MsgPack022.
attacks.result_detail: describes documented or already tested behaviour (MsgPack021 / MsgPack022 paths); no probe written

attacks.claim: Misuse of the attribute is reported as a compile error: a non-partial formatter (MsgPack019), a class that does not implement IMessagePackFormatter<T> (MsgPack020), an abstract type (MsgPack021) and surrogate mismatches (MsgPack022, MsgPack005).
A surrogate type's [Key] and [IgnoreMember] attributes decide which members are written and under which keys, with members matched by name and type.
attacks.scenario: The matching only checks name and type, not member kind. A field in the surrogate can successfully match a property in the formatted type.
attacks.test_sketch: Define `class T { public int Id { get; set; } }` and a surrogate `class Surrogate { [Key(0)] public int Id; }`. The generator accepts this and serializes the property.
attacks.result_detail: G2: a surrogate field matches a target property and the round trip works. Behaviour as described, not a defect. runs/2129/probe/G2_SurrogateFieldMatchesProperty.txt

attacks.claim: Adding the public attribute class GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute to the MessagePack.Annotations assembly is additive and does not change existing public API.
Custom formatters specified on surrogate members are ignored.
attacks.scenario: If a surrogate member is annotated with `[MessagePackFormatter]`, the generator ignores it and does not apply the custom formatter to the serialized member.
attacks.test_sketch: Define a surrogate with `[Key(0), MessagePackFormatter(typeof(CustomIntFormatter))] public int Id { get; set; }`. The generated formatter will use the default int formatter, not `CustomIntFormatter`.
attacks.result_detail: G3: [MessagePackFormatter(typeof(...))] on a surrogate member is ignored; wire shows [21], the doubling formatter would give [42]. runs/2129/probe/G3_CustomFormatterOnSurrogateMember.txt
